EDITSv1 E8.2. PUBLIC + STATE-CHANGING BY DESIGN, reviewed: a promotion on a public page is seen mostly by signed-out visitors and impressions are counted for them, so restricting clicks to signed-in users would leave the owner reading a click-through rate whose numerator is systematically missing. Blast radius is one integer: the handler can only add 1 to SiteAnnouncement.clicks on one row — it reads nothing, returns nothing about the campaign, and cannot reach any user's data. Protections: verifyOrigin (so another site cannot drive it from a visitor's browser) plus a hashed-IP limiter via checkAnonLimit (30 / 5min). rateLimit is 'none' here because that field tracks checkRateLimit/RATE_LIMITS keys only, per the auth/register precedent; the real limiter is src/lib/rate-limit.js's checkAnonLimit.

EDITSv1 E8.2: persists a signed-in user's dismissal so a campaign closed on one device stays closed on the next (it used to be localStorage-only). Auth required — an anonymous viewer has no account to hang the row off and keeps the localStorage path. Idempotent by construction via the (announcementId, userId) compound unique, so a double-submit is an update, not a duplicate or a 500.

EDITSv1 E8.2. PUBLIC + STATE-CHANGING BY DESIGN, reviewed — same rationale, protections and blast radius as the sibling /click route (one integer, SiteAnnouncement.impressions), open to anonymous callers because a click count without a matching impression count measures nothing. Kept OUT of GET /api/announcements deliberately: a mutating GET would be incremented by every prefetch and speculative fetch, inflating the count with views no human had. verifyOrigin plus checkAnonLimit (60 / 5min).

2026-08-08 Dev mode: failures of the last 14 days grouped by the RAW provider reason, with ids scrubbed so the same failure lands in the same bucket. The user is shown a branded message on purpose (it does not name the upstream provider); the operator needs the opposite and was getting the branded string too, so "An unexpected error occurred" covered eleven models and every distinct cause. Reports dispatched-vs-not per group, which is the difference between "we broke" and "they broke". Read-only.

2026-08-08: TWO gates now, not one. The hardcoded DEV_EMAILS allowlist is kept (it is the narrowest thing we have) AND requireAdminUser is enforced, so a stolen session for a non-admin account is not enough even if its address is on the list. A non-developer gets 404 rather than 403 — a tool nobody may use should not announce itself. `source` is checked against MANAGED_PROCESSES in source and passed as an argv element to execFile; it was once interpolated into a shell string, which is the exact shape of bug this surface is built to not have. Cross-app log sources removed: only this product's processes.

2026-08-08 Dev mode: pm2 status, and a FIXED verb (restart|reload|stop|start) on a FIXED process name. Nothing from the request is ever built into a command — pm2 is called with an argv array, the name is checked against MANAGED_PROCESSES in source, the verb against a set of four, and `delete` is deliberately absent. Stopping the app or the worker is refused: one takes this page down with it, the other strands every queued job. Gated by requireDeveloper (DEV_EMAILS + admin role); every action is written to the audit log with the actor's email.

2026-08-08 Dev mode: disk, memory, load, uptime, queue depth and the DEPLOYED COMMIT. Read-only. df/free/git are run with argv arrays and take no input from the request at all. The commit matters because 'I deployed that' and 'that is what is running' are different claims.

2026-08-08: `status=all` serves the studio's Runs view (failures included — a failure you cannot see is one you cannot learn from); cleared runs stay hidden unless includeHidden=1.

2026-08-08: stop a run. THREE honest outcomes, not one — cancelled outright with the reservation RELEASED (it never reached a provider, so nothing is owed), stopped-waiting-but-still-billed (it did reach one, and the provider charges us whether or not we listen), or too late. Reporting "cancelled" for the middle case would be a lie the user only discovers on their statement. Owner-scoped; a miss reads as not-found.
